title: add rdev_*() functions to check packages with two R builds
description:
First, a caveat: I understand entirely if this is not something you want to pull into revdepcheck. It adds a second mode to the package that serves a fairly specific need (testing local changes to R itself), and it is reasonable to say that belongs elsewhere. If that is the call, no hard feelings; we would still be glad to hear whether any of the smaller generic pieces are worth keeping on their own, and we are happy to maintain this as a fork or separate package instead.

## What this does

The `rdev_*()` functions run `R CMD check` on a set of CRAN packages with two builds of R and report the differences, reusing the `revdep_check()` machinery with the two R builds taking the place of the CRAN and development versions of a package. The intended use is checking a local change to R: build R once from the unmodified sources (the "old" build) and once with the change (the "new" build), then check the packages most likely to be affected.

```r
root <- "~/rcheck/my-branch"
rdev_init(root, r_old = "~/r/build-trunk/bin/R", r_new = "~/r/build-my-branch/bin/R")

# Specific packages, everything that depends on Rcpp, or both
rdev_add(root, packages = c("data.table", "dplyr"), revdeps_of = "Rcpp")

rdev_check(root, num_workers = 8)

# Rebuild the new R, then re-check what broke
rdev_add_broken(root)
rdev_check(root, num_workers = 8)
```

Reports (`README.md`, `problems.md`, `failures.md`) are written to the root, with the old build in the role of CRAN and the new build in the role of the development version. `rdev_summary()`, `rdev_details()`, `rdev_todo()`, `rdev_rm()`, `rdev_reset()` and `rdev_report()` mirror their `revdep_*()` counterparts.

## How it fits into the existing code

The scheduler, database, comparison and report code are reused unchanged apart from labels. The switch points are:

- `pkg_check()` and `dir_find()` accept a root marked by an `rdev.yml` file; the root itself is the check directory, and there is no old/new library for a package under test.
- The event loop carries an `rdev` option that the dependency-install, download and check tasks use to run under the chosen R binary.
- `revdep_report_summary()` shows an "R builds" table instead of the dependency table, and `cran.md` is skipped.

## Implementation notes

- **Checks run through a small processx-based process class** (`rdev_check_process`) rather than `rcmdcheck_process`. callr only honours its `arch` option for plain R processes; for `R CMD` processes it always starts the session's R, which we only discovered when the recorded check logs showed the wrong R version. The class keeps rcmdcheck's output accumulation and uses its (unexported) result constructor, which we would be glad to replace with an exported one.
- **Dependencies are installed by the old build into a shared per-package library.** This assumes the two builds share a `major.minor` and a compatible ABI, which is documented. crancache is installed into a private tools library with the old build, from its GitHub source since it is not on CRAN.
- **Build identity is a fingerprint** of the R path, version string, svn revision, and the newest mtime of the binaries and the base packages' lazy-load databases. A changed old build invalidates old results, the tools library and the default package cache.
- **Old-build results are reused across reruns** only when the package version and a recorded snapshot of the installed dependency versions match, so iterating on the new build only re-checks that side.
- **Worker processes set `R_LIBS_USER` and `R_LIBS_SITE` explicitly.** callr leaves the session's values in the child environment, and a devel build sharing a `major.minor` with the session's release R would otherwise load release-built packages and crash.
- **The package cache is warmed serially** before the parallel phase; several workers initialising an empty crancache at once raced on its metadata.
- **Package availability is judged without the session's `R_version` filter.** crancache's `available_packages()` cannot take explicit filters (its default handling has an operator-precedence problem), so `utils::available.packages()` is used when filters are needed.

## Changes outside the new feature

- `cran_revdeps()` gains an optional `filters` argument.
- Declared minimums: callr (>= 3.6.0), processx (>= 3.5.0), rcmdcheck (>= 1.4.0); R6 added to Imports.
- A two-line `@importFrom` in `R/cloud.R` was joined onto one line: roxygen2 8.x aborts on multi-line `@importFrom` tags, so documenting the package was impossible without it.
- `.worktrees` added to `.gitignore` and `.Rbuildignore`.

## Verification

- Unit tests cover root detection and layout, config, fingerprinting, reuse decisions and invalidation, the `check_done()` and `download_done()` state transitions, the process class (via a wrapper script that records being invoked), and worker options.
- End-to-end runs on macOS with two local R-devel builds (r90118 and r90424) checked `clisymbols` and `prettyunits` with two workers from an empty cache; each side's check log shows its own build, and re-checks reuse the old side as intended.

## Known limitations

- Builds with an incompatible ABI (changes to the C API, byte-code or serialization) need per-build libraries, which this does not implement.
- crancache is installed from its GitHub `HEAD`; pinning a ref would make tools libraries reproducible.
- `revdep_env_vars()` chooses the `_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_*` variable from the session's R rather than the builds under test.

title: Skip packages that fail to download instead of stopping
description:
When a package cannot be downloaded after 20 attempts (e.g., archived or unavailable packages), gracefully skip it and continue checking other packages instead of throwing a fatal error.

The failed package is:
- Marked as done with PREPERROR status in the database
- Recorded for both 'old' and 'new' checks
- Logged with an informative message

This follows the same pattern used in deps_install_done() for handling dependency installation failures.

Fixes #281

title: Update for modern gmailr
description:
Where modern means circa 2019

Fixes #402

In gmailr v1.0.0 (2019-08-23), approximately all functions in gmailr gained a `gm_` prefix to phase out horrible name collisions with, e.g., the base package. I'm talking about `base::body()` and `base::message()` and the like.

In the gmailr version I'm about to release, I finally remove all the old functions lacking the prefix.

I don't think this email-sending code really gets exercised here anymore (?), so this may be purely academic. But it's necessary to keep revdepcheck usable.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to revdepcheck website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the revdepcheck website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

## Screenshots

At 1200px browser width:

![Screenshot of revdepcheck website at 1200px browser width](https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/screenshots/revdepcheck-1200.png)

title: More resilient reporting when revdep's DESCRIPTION is missing or empty
description:
Fixes #295, fixes #310

I had a very conservative goal here: replace the `NA`s we see for problem packages in `cloud_summary()`, `revdep/README.md` and `revdep/failures.md` with a package name. I have succeeded in this.

There are still quite a few problems with how these problem packages are being reported (or, rather, are not necessarily being reported), but I think other issues already capture some of the more substantive problems (such as #317, #301). 

I was developing against a specific cloud revdep run for usethis, so I had authentic weird stuff to work with. All the `NA`s in my case were due to `DESCRIPTION` being non-existent or empty, for a revdep package. That was explained by the package being on Bioconductor, not CRAN, or requiring a higher R version than we were checking with. Or because shit happens? There was at least one package that had bizarre results for no identifiable reason and this self-resolved in a future revdep run.

title: Handle groups in revdep_report_cran()
description:
Includes #167 

- Use the `repo` column to determine CRAN packages
- Indicate to user what groups (other than `repo`) the summary aggregates over
- Add `groups` argument to specify levels to summarise in

Example:

  ```
  revdep_report_cran(path)
  #> The summary aggregates over the following groups:
  #>
  #> # A tibble: 2 x 1
  #>   set
  #>   <chr>
  #> 1 rlang
  #> 2 purrr
  #>
  #> Pass `groups` to specify group levels to summarise in.
  #>
  #> ## revdepcheck results
  #>
  #> We checked 6 reverse dependencies (4 from CRAN + 2 from
  #> BioConductor), comparing R CMD check results across CRAN and dev
  #> versions of this package.
  #>
  #>  * We saw 0 new problems
  #>  * We failed to check 3 packages
  #>
  #> Issues with CRAN packages are summarised below.
  #>
  #> ### Failed to check
  #>
  #> * AMR        (failed to install)
  #> * amt        (failed to install)
  #> * adaptalint (failed to install)
  ```

Then, to summarise within a specific set:

  ```
  revdep_report_cran(path, c(set = "rlang"))
  #> ## revdepcheck results
  #>
  #> We checked 2 reverse dependencies, comparing R CMD check results
  #> across CRAN and dev versions of this package.
  #>
  #>  * We saw 0 new problems
  #>  * We failed to check 2 packages
  #>
  #> Issues with CRAN packages are summarised below.
  #>
  #> ### Failed to check
  #>
  #> * AMR (failed to install)
  #> * mt (failed to install)
  ```

title: Add revdep_pkgs() to create sets of packages to test
description:
Includes #166

Implements the user-facing changes of the group support.

* The `bioc` and `dependencies` arguments of `revdep_check()` are now deprecated and replaced by a `revdeps` argument.

* `revdep_pkgs()` creates a tibble of packages. It always includes a `repo` column. You can pass several packages to check the revdeps of, in which case a column `set` is added to match the revdeps to their package. These columns are interpreted as groups by the new DB code.

  If you pass `NULL` instead, you get all packages from CRAN (and Bioconductor if `bioc` is `TRUE`). You can then use dplyr `group_by()` + `sample_n()` to get a random sample of packages. This will be useful for testing patches to R.

  Duplicated packages are removed so only the union of the revdeps is returned.

title: Add support for groups in database
description:
Includes #164 

* `db_todo_add()` now takes a tibble instead of a character vector. The tibble must have a `package` column. Any other columns are taken to define groups. This is the data structure that the upcoming `revdep_pkgs()` function will return. It is validated by `pkgs_validate()`.

  Example with two grouping variables `set` and `repo`:

  ```
  #> # A tibble: 8 x 3
  #>   set   repo     package
  #> * <chr> <chr>    <chr>
  #> 1 rlang CRAN     AMR
  #> 2 rlang CRAN     amt
  #> 3 rlang BioCsoft biovizBase
  #> 4 rlang BioCsoft COMPASS
  #> 5 purrr CRAN     abjutils
  #> 6 purrr CRAN     adaptalint
  #> 7 purrr BioCsoft CNPBayes
  #> 8 purrr BioCsoft DChIPRep
  ```

  This tibble is merged with existing groups to make it easy to add packages back to the TODO table manually without having to provide their groups again.

* The unique combinations of groups are stored in a new table `groups` in the database. The new `db_groups()` function returns a tibble of groups and packages.

* `db_todo()` returns the TODO packages joined on their group.

* `db_results()` returns a tibble with 5 columns: `package`, `groups` (a df-col of multiple columns), `old`, `new`, and `comparisons`.

  `old`, `new`, and `comparisons` are returned as a list-columns that are easy to map over. `groups` is a data frame column that can contain as many grouping variables as was entered by the user. All these data structures are properly joined on `package`.

  ```
  # A tibble: 2 x 5
    package   groups$set $repo old            new           comparisons
    <chr>     <chr>      <chr> <list>         <list>        <list>
  1 abjutils  rlang      CRAN  <tibble [1 × … <tibble [1 ×… <S3: rcmdcheck_compar…
  2 ActisoftR purrr      CRAN  <tibble [1 × … <tibble [1 ×… <S3: rcmdcheck_compar…
  ```

The following changes were made to help unit testing:

* `db_metadata_init()` accepts `":memory:"` as package name
* `db()` is now a noop with connections.
* Default `revdeps` option for `db_get_results()`
* Fake package in the fixtures folder

title: Add data frame join infrastructure
description:
These are supporting functions for joining the group data frames in upcoming PRs. Requires dev version of tibble for df-col support.

The motivation for `join()` is that joining the groups as a df-col makes it possible for the groups to have arbitrary number of columns with minimal bookkeeping, while matching the rows on `package`. It also makes it easy to join as list-columns which are suitable for mapping over.

title: Require processx >= 3.0.1
description:
Closes #129

revdepcheck assumes existence of the `read_output()` and `read_error()` process methods which are only present in recent versions.

title: memoise available_packages()
description:
Makes the event loop much much smoother, but still not sufficient for 64 cores. I suspect in this scenario many workers are working on building/installing the same packages, also I/O queues might overflow.

Maybe it's also just the effort of reinstalling BH all over again.

title: Various minor fixes for reporting
description:
"Hammer style", because I wasn't sure about the code design. I think we could use a new class that wraps both `"rcmdcheck_comparison"` and allows capturing errors, timeouts etc. if we don't compare.

- Packages where the internal results are of class `"rcmdcheck_error"` are considered broken, for reporting the stdout and stderr for old and new are printed.
- These packages show with version = NA in the list, I'm sure we can do better here.
- Fixed adding broken packages.

title: Only update progress bar if we are not completed.
